experiments.name: SSITKA Operando DRIFTS (12CO to 13CO Formate Exchange)
experiments.description: Steady-State Isotopic Transient Kinetic Analysis swapping 12CO for 13CO while monitoring the decay of 12C-formates vs production of 13CO2 via operando DRIFTS-MS at 200°C.

predictions.basis: In Redox mechanism, reaction bypasses formates entirely; surface formates are spectators and exchange much slower than TOF (r_for/TOF = 0.14 from CLM-WGS-001). Small 0.04 probability accounts for minority fast-exchange pool or detector drift.
Matches empirical observation from Kalamaras et al. (2011) Table 2 where measured formate exchange is 7x slower than TOF.
If formates are the primary intermediate, their consumption rate must balance the steady-state CO2 turnover frequency (r_for ~ TOF). Residual 0.06 reflects experimental transient dispersion.
Small probability account for minority slow-exchange pools.
Under carboxyl mechanism, formates are spectator pools; exchange rate does not match catalytic turnover.
Consistent with carboxyl pathway prediction where reaction flux bypasses formate reservoir.

assumptions: Negligible gas-phase holdup dispersion in transient cell (<0.5 s dead time)
Linear relationship between DRIFTS peak area and surface formate coverage

experiments.name: Transient H2(18O) / C(16O) Isotopic Pulse Mass Spectrometry
experiments.description: Pre-equilibrate catalyst in H2(18O), then pulse C(16O) and measure mass-to-charge ratios m/z 44 (C16O2), m/z 46 (C16O18O), and m/z 48 (C18O2) to determine the origin of oxygen in initial CO2 product.

predictions.basis: In Mars-van Krevelen redox, CO abstracts native support lattice oxygen (16O) leaving a vacancy, before 18O replenishes it. Measured initial 16O fraction was 88% (CLM-WGS-002).
Minor surface 18O exchange prior to pulse.
Associative mechanism requires OH from water; if water is 18O-labeled, initial product must be C16O18O.
Direct coupling with 18O-hydroxyls yields C16O18O.
Active carboxyl from 18O-hydroxyls yields C16O18O; minor 16O exchange from support.
Direct carboxyl pathway incorporates oxygen from dissociated water (18O).

assumptions: Rapid baseline stabilization without pre-reduction artifacts

experiments.name: Operando Ambient-Pressure Ce L3-edge XAS (Ce3+ Vacancy Tracking)
experiments.description: Synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy measuring the Ce3+ / Ce4+ edge shift under steady-state reaction conditions (200°C, 1 bar CO/H2O mix) to quantify dynamic oxygen vacancies.

predictions.basis: Redox cycle continuously generates and fills oxygen vacancies at Pt-ceria perimeter, establishing measurable steady-state Ce3+ concentration (8-10% from CLM-WGS-005).
Signal attenuation in thick catalyst beds.
Minor background reduction in dry CO feed.
Pure associative mechanism does not rely on lattice vacancy generation; ceria acts as static hydroxyl donor.
Slight vacancy modulation near Pt perimeter during transient startup.
Associative carboxyl route primarily involves surface hydroxyl groups without extensive lattice oxygen turnover.

assumptions: AP-XAS reaction cell windows withstand 1 bar reaction pressure at 200°C

experiments.name: Steady-State H2O / D2O Kinetic Isotope Effect (KIE: r_H / r_D)
experiments.description: Measure steady-state catalytic reaction rate with H2O vs D2O at 200°C to determine primary vs secondary kinetic isotope effect.

predictions.basis: Redox rate-determining step is CO reduction of lattice oxygen; water re-oxidation step is fast, yielding modest secondary KIE (1.1-1.3 from CLM-WGS-004).
Experimental error / transport limitation.
Unexpected for C-H bond cleavage.
Formate decomposition involves C-H (or C-D) bond scission in the rate-determining step, producing a pronounced primary KIE (>= 1.8).
Carboxyl decomposition involves O-H bond cleavage with moderate theoretical KIE (1.2-1.5).
Possible transition state isotope effects.

assumptions: Differential conversion regime maintained (<10% conversion) to avoid thermodynamic back-reaction

experiments.name: Operando Sub-Second Stopped-Flow Carboxyl Detection (Proposed)
experiments.description: Sub-second rapid-scan ATR-SEIRAS targeting transient carboxyl (*COOH) stretching bands at 1690 cm^-1.
assumptions: Unquantified in current published literature: *COOH lifetime is estimated at <10 microseconds, below current signal-to-noise ratio. Likelihood distributions cannot be fabricated without active measurement.
